ai.description: *Eutropis carinata* reaches 13 cm snout-vent length. It is bronze-brown with dark lateral stripes and distinct keeled scales. A pale dorsolateral stripe often extends from the head to the tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: Distinguish *Eutropis carinata* by the three distinct, strongly keeled longitudinal ridges running along the dorsal scales, which feel rough to the touch compared to smoother skinks.
ai.habitat: *Eutropis carinata* inhabits diverse environments, ranging from moist deciduous forests and scrublands to gardens, typically at elevations from sea level up to 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Keeled Indian Mabuya is primarily diurnal and often basks on rocks or walls to regulate its body temperature before actively foraging for insects and small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eutropis carinata* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 5–12 eggs. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eutropis carinata* is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from sea level to 2,000 meters in diverse habitats across most Indian states.
